target.statement: KNM with Cauchy kernel achieves up to 99.1% accuracy on the F2 (feedback sensor) fault scenario under IPPT mode using four variables (Ipv, Vpv, Vdc, Vf)
target.table_ref: Abstract / Section 3 results (accuracy for F2, Cauchy kernel)
target.dataset: GPVS-Faults (Mendeley Data, Bakdi et al. 2020), IPPT mode, F2 fault

compute.basis: No code released, so the full KNM pipeline (sliding windows, DFT feature extraction, kernel grid search, Frobenius-norm statistic, thresholding, plus OCSVM/iForest/LOF baselines) must be reimplemented from the text; data are ~100 kHz time series but only 4 variables and short 10-15 s experiments, so CPU-only compute is modest; most time is reimplementation and debugging, not runtime.

blockers: No code or configs released; method must be reimplemented from prose
Some protocol details (window length w, step s, number of Fourier components I, grid Gamma, baseline length) are only partially specified
High-frequency (~100 kHz) raw data require careful windowing/FFT handling to match reported accuracy
title: An unsupervised kernel norm monitoring for fault detection in a time series photovoltaic system
